title: The Investor's Edge Lives in Their Head — Anekha Sokhal, Moshi
talk_summary: A fintech founder argues that AI should not replace human judgment but should handle the 'grind' (data gathering, cleaning, cross-checking) while humans make decisions, and that trustworthiness requires measuring hallucination and tracing every claim. The talk is mostly market positioning for Moshi, a 24/7 quant analyst product, with little concrete engineering detail.

takeaways.what_they_do: They measure every claim the agent produces, check whether it is traceable to a source, and surface the assumptions that led to a conclusion so users can audit the reasoning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We measure the hallucination, we measure every claim, we see how it's traceable, and we also give the user the assumptions

takeaways.technique: Split grind from judgment across deterministic agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They run a team of six agents built deterministically to do the reading/gathering/cleaning grind 24/7, and deliberately leave the final decision to the human rather than letting agents close the loop.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are running a team of six different agents, which are built in a deterministic manner, which are watching the market 24/7

takeaways.technique: Push context to the human instead of pull
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue push-based delivery of new, relevant information (blind spots, divergences) is more valuable than pull-based prompting of a frozen model, because it forces new connections and surfaces what the user would not have asked for.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you are getting pushed new data, it's forcing your brain to think about new things and make connections

takeaways.technique: Separate context problem from data-volume problem
takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish tools you pull data from (a context problem: you must explain everything to a frozen model) from tools that push data to you (a data-engineering problem: flooding), and treat them with different mechanisms.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one is context, and then the other one is the amount of data
